title: Compression test and cylinder leak-down test
warnings: Disable fuel and ignition before cranking
During leak-down the engine can spin hard when air goes in. Keep hands clear and hold the crank.
steps: Warm engine if possible. Remove all spark plugs. Disable fuel and ignition. Block the throttle wide open.
Thread the gauge in one cylinder, crank 4-6 compression strokes, record the reading. Repeat for all cylinders.
Healthy engines read within about 10-15% of each other. The absolute number varies by engine.
A low cylinder: squirt a teaspoon of oil in and retest. Number comes up = rings. Stays low = valves or head gasket.
Two adjacent cylinders both low = likely head gasket between them.
For a leak-down, bring the low cylinder to TDC on compression, connect the tester and apply regulated air.
Listen for where the air escapes: intake (throttle body/carb) = intake valve, tailpipe = exhaust valve, oil fill/dipstick = rings, bubbles in radiator = head gasket or cracked head.
Under 10% leakage is good; 10-20% fair; over 20-30% needs attention.
